record.original_question:
A function ψ on R^n is r-regular for r = 0,1,2,… or ∞ if ψ is C^r and all partial derivatives up to order r decay polynomially: ∂^α ψ(x) = O(|x|^{−N}) as |x|→∞ for all |α| ≤ r, for some N>0.

Does there exist an ∞-regular wavelet construction in higher dimensions?

evidence.quote:
well-localized wavelets are r-regular wavelets introduced by Meyer [48]. We recall that a
function ψ is r-regular, where r = 0, 1, 2, . . ., or ∞, if ψ is C r with polynomially decaying
partial derivatives of orders ≤ r,

                 ∂ α ψ(x) = O(|x|−N ) as |x| → ∞           for all |α| ≤ r, N > 0.

   For any integer dilation A, which supports a self-similar tiling of Rn , Strichartz [60] con-
structed r-regular wavelets for all r ∈ N. However, there are examples in R4 of dilation
matrices without self-similar tiling [41, 42]. In [7] the first author has shown that for every
integer dilation and r ∈ N, there is an r-regular wavelet basis with an associated r-regular
multiresolution analysis. However, the question of existence of ∞-regular wavelets in higher
dimensions is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For r ∈ {0, 1, 2, …} ∪ {∞}, call a function ψ : ℝⁿ → ℂ r-regular if ψ ∈ C^r(ℝⁿ) and, for every multi-index α with |α| ≤ r and every N > 0, the partial derivatives satisfy
   ∂^α ψ(x) = O(|x|^{−N}) as |x| → ∞.

Let n ≥ 2 and let A be an n × n integer matrix that is expansive (i.e., all eigenvalues of A have modulus strictly greater than 1). A wavelet basis associated with the dilation A is a finite family {ψ¹, …, ψ^L} ⊂ L²(ℝⁿ) such that the system
   { |det A|^{j/2} ψ^ℓ(A^j x − k) : 1 ≤ ℓ ≤ L, j ∈ ℤ, k ∈ ℤⁿ }
forms an orthonormal basis of L²(ℝⁿ).

Question: For every expansive integer dilation matrix A on ℝⁿ (in particular in dimensions n ≥ 3, including cases where A admits no self-similar tiling of ℝⁿ), does there exist a wavelet basis {ψ¹, …, ψ^L} associated with A such that each generator ψ^ℓ is ∞-regular?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 paper on Meyer wavelets for rational dilations explicitly states that the existence problem for ∞-regular (Meyer) wavelets associated with integer dilations remains open in dimensions ≥ 3, while it is resolved for n = 2 and for rational dilations in any dimension. Bownik's open-problems list in wavelet theory also lists the higher-dimensional integer-dilation case as outstanding.

status_evidence.title: Meyer wavelets for rational dilations
status_evidence.snippet: the problem of characterizing dilations A for which there exist Meyer wavelets with a minimal number of generators remains open in dimensions ≥3 for integer dilations
status_evidence.claim: As of 2025, existence of ∞-regular Meyer wavelets for integer dilations in dimensions ≥ 3 is still open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Wavelet Theory (Bownik)
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems list including existence of well-localized (r-regular, ∞-regular) wavelets for general expansive dilations in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: The question is listed among open problems in wavelet theory.
